question: A previously healthy 16-year-old boy comes to the physician because of a pruritic rash on the chest that has become progressively larger over the past 10 days. It is not painful. He is sexually active with two female partners and uses condoms inconsistently. He works part-time as a lifeguard. He has no family history of serious illness. He does not smoke. He drinks 5–6 beers on weekends. His temperature is 36.7°C (98°F), pulse is 66/min, and blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg. A photograph of the rash is shown below. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Pruritic rash on the chest -> progressively larger over 10 days -> not painful -> sexually active with two female partners -> inconsistent condom use -> part-time lifeguard -> no family history of serious illness -> non-smoker -> drinks 5-6 beers on weekends -> vital signs stable -> temperature 36.7°C (98°F) -> pulse 66/min -> blood pressure 110/70 mm Hg -> next step: further evaluation for sexually transmitted infections (STIs) -> 85%
analysis: Based on the presentation of a pruritic rash on the chest of a sexually active teenager with inconsistent condom use, working as a lifeguard, and alcohol consumption, the most appropriate next step would be to perform testing for sexually transmitted infections (STIs) given the risk factors involved.
